This was a common problem for aspiring programmers: The gulf between learning and doing. Learners would read about programming, then reach for their code, wondering, "Now what?"
bridges this divide, providing small, digestible quiz questions with immediate answers, AI-generated explanations and
reward feature to pull users back day after day.

Beginners and intermediate learners can use the platform because it is designed to have learning going both ways. Each design choice, ranging from simplified quiz styles to a helpful AI guide, is based on the mission to minimise friction and increase engagement in self-directed programming education.

The above tiered access model is echoed throughout the platforms access control system, guest users access to a focused publicly accessible home page, learning members access to the full feature (quiz/reward capability) personal dashboard and admins have access to content/user management console. Designing specifically for each audience (using, learning members and admins) and what that audience will aspire to achieve from the platform as opposed to using a “cookie cutter” design approach follows fundamental usability guidelines.

The application stores all the necessary data in a single MySQL database that has logically separated tables for application data and user activities. The CRUD operations necessary and defined for our application can be found and demonstrated with good example use-cases through the application:
Register the learner user, submit quiz, add a question to a quiz.
List leaderboard; render quiz questions, score list history; display learner profile, admin user table.
Update learner user info, edit an existing question, update streaks in background process on a daily basis.
delete a question or group that is out of date delete a learner account.
Major database tables used are User (or Users), Role (or Roles), Question (or Questions), Category (or Categories),
). ERD and entire Schema will be defined in Design stage and included in report.
